brief: Eight money mistakes solo founders make in year one. Each row: the mistake, the real cost, the simple fix.

slots.desc1: Mixing personal and business spend from day one.
slots.desc2: Chasing vanity metrics while cash flow quietly crumbles.
slots.desc3: Hiring contractors without contracts or clear scope.
slots.desc4: Paying everyone except yourself until burnout hits.
slots.desc5: Pouring budget into branding before real sales exist.

slots.toolTagline: Using one account for personal and business spending.
slots.bigStatement: Real cost: Missed deductions and a tax-season nightmare that eats weeks.
slots.use1Body: You swipe one card for coffee and cloud hosting alike.
slots.use2Body: Accountants charge extra to untangle twelve months of messy transactions.
slots.use3Body: Open a free business checking account before your next expense.

slots.toolTagline: Obsessing over followers while your runway quietly evaporates.
slots.bigStatement: Real cost: A payroll crisis that forces desperate, dilutive fundraising.
slots.use1Body: You celebrate social growth while invoices sit unpaid for months.
slots.use2Body: You miss payroll and lose talent you spent months recruiting.
slots.use3Body: Review cash flow weekly and chase invoices like they are leads.

slots.toolTagline: Bringing on help without contracts, scopes, or vesting schedules.
slots.bigStatement: Real cost: Legal disputes and spend on work you cannot legally ship.
slots.use1Body: You onboard a dev with a handshake deal and no IP assignment.
slots.use2Body: They claim equity or you rewrite code you already paid for.
slots.use3Body: Sign a SOW with IP clauses before any work officially begins.

slots.toolTagline: Reinvesting every dollar while you live on stress and ramen.
slots.bigStatement: Real cost: Burnout-induced decision paralysis that stalls the company for months.
slots.use1Body: You skip draws for six months to keep the burn rate low.
slots.use2Body: Exhaustion makes you avoid sales calls and key product choices.
slots.use3Body: Set a modest monthly draw and treat it as non-negotiable overhead.

slots.toolTagline: Spending thousands on a logo before you have ten paying customers.
slots.bigStatement: Real cost: A beautiful site selling a product nobody actually asked for.
slots.use1Body: You order custom packaging while your MVP still has critical bugs.
slots.use2Body: Polish masks weak product-market fit and delays honest customer feedback.
slots.use3Body: Sell with a plain landing page; invest in design after repeat revenue.

slots.toolTagline: Forgetting the IRS and spending every dollar that hits your account.
slots.bigStatement: Real cost: A five-figure April bill with penalties you cannot negotiate away.
slots.use1Body: You treat gross revenue like it is yours to spend freely.
slots.use2Body: Quarterly penalties and a lump sum that wipes out your cushion.
slots.use3Body: Auto-transfer thirty percent of profit to a separate tax savings account.

slots.body: Year one is about survival, not perfection. Fix your finances now and ship with confidence.
slots.signoff: keep your cash and your sanity
